column3: NASB follows the critical text, a shorter prayer: “Father,” without “our … in heaven” and without “Your will be done, on earth as in heaven.”
NASB follows the critical text without “but deliver us from evil.”
NASB recasts the question as “Suppose one of you has a friend.”
NASB adds “anything”; “persistence” renders a word that may also mean “shamelessness.”
NASB follows the critical text (only the fish and snake) and recasts the question in the passive.
NASB follows the critical text and recasts the question.
NASB renders “the Father from heaven” as “your heavenly Father.”
NASB follows the critical text; “prince” is rendered “ruler.”
NASB renders “a house against a house falls” as “a house divided against itself falls.”
NASB follows the critical text; “divides” is rendered “distributes.”
NASB lacks “unoccupied,” a word found in some manuscripts but not in the critical text.
“Rather” is rendered “On the contrary,” and “keeping” is “observe.”
